title: Nissanka Senadhipathi appears before Bribery Commission
byline: Nissanka Senadhipathi, former Chairman of Avant-Garde Maritime Services, appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning.

title: Canada flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seat belt
byline: The cancellation of a flight in Canada after a child refused to wear a seat belt has reignited a debate about the etiquette and safety procedures relating to children travelling on planes.

title: President to meet BASL over proposed judicial retirement age changes
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is scheduled to meet representatives of the Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) tomorrow to discuss the proposed constitutional amendment concerning the retirement age of judges.

title: Sri Lanka moves to strengthen regulation and welfare of captive elephants
byline: The Government is taking steps to introduce a stronger regulatory framework for captive elephants in Sri Lanka, including their use in cultural and religious pageants.

title: Immigration Department system restored after morning breakdown
byline: The computer system of the Immigration and Emigration Department, which experienced a sudden breakdown this morning (11), has now been restored, officials said.

title: Two arrested with protected animal parts in Kuruwita raid
byline: Two suspects have been arrested with a large quantity of highly protected animal parts during a surprise raid in the Paradise area of the Kuruwita Police Division yesterday (10), based on intelligence provided by the Sri Lanka Air Force.

title: Mobile hospital service planned to provide emergency care for wild elephants
byline: A dedicated mobile hospital service for wild elephants is being established by the Department of Wildlife Conservation to provide faster medical treatment to injured and sick elephants in remote areas.

title: Immigration system outage disrupts one-day passport service
byline: The one-day service system of Sri Lanka’s Department of Immigration and Emigration has experienced a technical disruption, hindering the issuance of passports and other travel documents.

title: At least 132 killed in Colombia’s largest earthquake in years
byline: At least 132 people are dead and a state of emergency has been declared after Colombia was hit by one of its largest earthquakes in years.

title: All the box-office records ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ has broken so far
byline:
Adding to its record tally, Spider-Man: Brand New Day has become the highest-grossing Hollywood film of all time in India, taking $10.6 million over the weekend for a cumulative $52.8 million.
Spider-Man, Spider-Man, breaks (almost) all the box office records a movie can.

title: Budget Proposals Hub of Verité Research returns ahead of Budget 2027
byline: Verité Research has launched the second edition of its pioneering Budget Proposals Hub, inviting citizens, residents, and organisations to submit proposals for the government’s consideration ahead of the 2027 national budget.

title: China says Long March 7A rocket launch failed after flight anomaly
byline: China said a Long March 7A rocket carrying the ​ChinaSat-4B satellite failed after an in-flight anomaly following liftoff from the Wenchang space launch site in the southern island province ‌of Hainan on Monday.

title: Health Ministry still silent over Ratnapura patient’s death
byline: After over a month, the Health Ministry has yet to respond to a complaint seeking an independent investigation into the death of a 21-year-old woman at the Ratnapura General Hospital, amid allegations of possible medical negligence.

title: Police on alert for underworld retaliation following Maligawatta shooting
byline: Police are on alert over possible retaliatory underworld activity following yesterday’s fatal shooting on Sangharaja Mawatha in Maligawatta, in which a close relative of underworld figure Kanjipani Imran was shot dead.

title: Which teams have qualified for 2027 ODI Cricket World Cup so far?
byline: Afghanistan secured an automatic qualification into the 2027 World Cup after the Rahmat Shah-led side defeated Ireland by three wickets in the third ODI in Belfast on Monday. In the process, Afghanistan lead the series 2-0 after the first game ended in a washout.

title: 22A poses serious threat to democracy: GL
byline: The proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution poses a serious threat to human rights, the role of the Opposition and Sri Lanka’s democratic institutions, former Foreign Minister Prof. G.L. Peiris has warned.

title: Specialist doctor-Acting Deputy Director row over alleged scratching
byline: A dispute between a specialist doctor and the acting Deputy Director of Sri Jayawardenapura General Hospital has been referred to a mediation board following complaints made to the Welikada Police.

title: Sri Lankan Consulate to hold mobile service in Bern
byline: The Consulate General of Sri Lanka in Switzerland will conduct a two-day Consular Mobile Service in Bern on August 29 and 30, 2026, to provide essential consular services to Sri Lankan expatriates living in Bern and surrounding areas.

title: Farmer’s fight over water supply ends in Supreme Court after 20 years
byline: The Supreme Court has dismissed a nearly 20-year-old legal battle instituted by a farmer in Aralaganwila, Polonnaruwa against a local Govi Sanvidanaya after the organisation temporarily cut off the water supply to his paddy field over a Rs. 15,000 loan default.

title: US judge dismisses criminal case against Indian billionaire Adani
byline: A U.S. judge on Monday ​dismissed criminal charges against Indian billionaire Gautam Adani, but said the Justice Department’s decision to abandon the fraud and bribery case was concerning.

title: Cabinet approves coconut land rehabilitation programme
byline: The Cabinet has approved a special coconut land rehabilitation programme aimed at increasing coconut production and promoting sustainable cultivation practices amid concerns over a possible El Niño condition in the coming months.

title: ‘Sumana’ becomes Pinnawala attraction
byline: A majestic elephant named “Sumana” has become one of the most eye-catching attractions for visitors to the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage.

title: Jaffna MC members protest against commissioner’s interference
byline: Jaffna Municipal Council members today staged a protest, accusing the Municipal Commissioner and other government officials of continuously obstructing the activities of the council’s elected representatives.

title: Trump hidden in catering truck in secret plane swap over Iran threat, reports say
byline: Donald Trump secretly swapped planes as he left a Nato summit in Turkey last month in response to a possible Iranian threat, US media report.

title: Let Sri Lankan wild elephant become national animal: Sajith
byline: Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa today called for the recognition of the Sri Lankan wild elephant as the country’s national animal and called for a scientific approach to resolve the human-elephant conflict.

title: Former Syrian President Assad sentenced to death in absentia
byline: A Syrian court sentenced in absentia ousted Syrian President Bashar al-Assad along with his younger brother to death on Tuesday for crimes against humanity and war crimes during Syria’s 14-year conflict that left about half a million people dead.

title: World Bank approves US$100 mn for North, East development programme
byline: The Cabinet has approved the signing of financial agreements to secure a US$100 million facility from the World Bank’s International Development Association (IDA) to implement an integrated regional development programme in Sri Lanka’s Northern and Eastern Provinces.

title: 30,000 MT of paddy to be converted into rice for market
byline: The Cabinet has approved a plan to convert 30,000 metric tonnes of paddy held by the Paddy Marketing Board into rice and release it to the market.

title: Rs. 1.2 bn approved for expressway maintenance
byline: The Cabinet has approved the purchase of new vehicles and machinery worth an estimated Rs. 1.2 billion for the operation and maintenance of Sri Lanka’s expressways.

title: $2.73 million project approved to improve maternal and child nutrition
byline: The Cabinet has approved a three-year project to improve nutrition services for pregnant and breastfeeding mothers and children under five in four districts.

title: Cabinet approves coal supply contracts for Lakvijaya Power Plant
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the award of contracts to two companies to supply coal to the Lakvijaya Power Plant in Norochcholai for the 2026/2027 period.

title: Rs. 232 mn allocated to restore 144 disaster-affected sacred sites
byline: The Cabinet has approved a proposal to allocate Rs. 232.07 million to renovate 144 additional religious sites damaged by various disasters caused by the ‘Ditwa’ disaster.

title: Muthurajawela to get three new fuel tanks
byline: The Cabinet has approved the award of a contract for the construction of three new fuel storage tanks at the Muthurajawela Terminal, aimed at strengthening Sri Lanka’s fuel storage capacity.

title: Cabinet nod to amend Fishermen’s Pension Scheme Act
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to amend the Fishermen’s Pension and Social Security Benefits Scheme Act, No. 23 of 1990, to better meet the current needs of the fishing community.

title: New DG appointed to National Botanic Gardens
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the permanent appointment of H. C. P. Jayaweera as Director General of the Department of National Botanic Gardens.

title: Rough seas, strong winds expected along several coasts
byline: The Department of Meteorology has issued an “Amber” advisory for strong winds and rough seas in several sea areas around Sri Lanka.

title: CAA conducts islandwide raids on Atapirikara, Pirikara sales
byline: The Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) has conducted a special islandwide raid targeting establishments selling Atapirikara and Pirikara items, uncovering several irregularities including incomplete sets and substandard items.

title: New zero-click WhatsApp attack raises concerns for iPhone users in Sri Lanka
byline: A newly identified zero-click cyberattack targeting WhatsApp users has raised concerns among iPhone users in Sri Lanka, with several individuals reportedly complaining to the Sri Lanka Computer Emergency Readiness Team (Sri Lanka CERT) after their accounts were compromised.

title: BASL rejects allegations by Jagath Abeynayaka over discussions on extending judges’ tenure
byline: The Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) rejected concerns raised by Attorney-at-Law Jagath Abeynayaka regarding the BASL’s discussions on the proposed extension of the retirement age of Supreme Court and Court of Appeal judges, while urging him to raise such matters through the Association’s established institutional processes.

title: New Chinese Envoy arrives, vows to strengthen bilateral ties
byline: Newly appointed Chinese Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to Sri Lanka, H.E. Wei Huaxiang, arrived in Sri Lanka to assume his post, pledging to strengthen the longstanding friendship and expand mutually beneficial cooperation between China and Sri Lanka.

title: Prison officer arrested over drug supply to Magazine Prison
byline: A prison officer suspected of supplying drugs to the Magazine Prison in Borella has been arrested by the Mount Lavinia Divisional Crime Investigation Bureau.

title: Six-planet parade to grace Sri Lankan skies
byline: Six planets—Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune—are expected to form an arc across the eastern and southern sky before sunrise tomorrow (12), the Astronomy Division of the Arthur C. Clarke Institute for Modern Technologies said.

title: CSE snaps four-day winning streak as indices edge lower
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange closed marginally lower on Tuesday, 11 August 2026, bringing an end to the ASPI’s four-session winning streak as buying momentum weakened during the day.

title: Six State bungalows up for 30-year commercial leases
byline: The Government has invited investment proposals from the private sector to commercially develop and operate several State-owned bungalows in Colombo under 30-year lease agreements.

title: Govt briefs Chief Prelates on judicial reform programme
byline: Responding to reports of a letter sent to the President opposing the proposed constitutional amendment to extend the retirement age of judges, Cabinet Spokesman Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said that the Government has briefed the Chief Prelates of three Nikayas on its proposed judicial reform programme.

title: Cabinet approves return of Sri Lankan refugees from India
byline: The Cabinet has approved measures to facilitate the voluntary return of Sri Lankans who fled to India during the war and were subsequently registered as refugees, allowing them to return through approved ports without facing legal action under the Immigration and Emigration Act.

title: Biometric system proposed for future electronic passports
byline: The provision is aimed at facilitating the implementation of a biometric data entry system for electronic passports to be issued in the future, under a new Immigration Bill approved by the Cabinet.

title: Minister’s brother-in-law arrested over alleged fraud
byline: The Kegalle Fraud Investigation Bureau has arrested the 59-year-old brother-in-law of Minister K.D. Lal Kantha in connection with an alleged financial fraud involving a vehicle auction.

title: CCCC explores further investment opportunities in Sri Lanka
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake met a senior delegation from China Communications Construction Company Limited (CCCC), led by Zhang Bingnan, at the Presidential Secretariat this afternoon (11), with discussions focusing on ongoing and proposed projects related to Colombo Port City.
